bug_description.normalized: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_33094/poc` is a 62-byte WebAssembly binary (sha256 `27d9843ed864920ccc007891e5f23e4c87e9fe3672cc5518683e02b82b10aa76`) that begins with the standard wasm magic/version header and reaches `ParseSection_Global()` during `m3_ParseModule()`. `Parse_InitExpr()` is then used only to walk the current global initializer to its terminating `end`; its own comment says this path "doesn't generate code pages", and line 280 materializes a parser-only `M3Compilation` whose `runtime` and `function` fields are NULL while `wasm` points at the attacker-controlled initializer bytes. In the staged vulnerable source, `Compile_BlockStatements()` reads opcode bytes from that initializer but performs no expression-opcode restriction before dispatching compiler helpers, so a witness `if` is sent to `Compile_If()` instead of being rejected with `m3Err_restictedOpcode`. Inside the nested `CompileBlock()` walk for the then arm, `Compile_BlockStatements()` later decodes `c_waOp_else`, stores it in `o->previousOpcode`, and breaks; when control returns, `Compile_If()` takes `if (o->previousOpcode == c_waOp_else)` and calls `CompileElseBlock()`. That path requests a fresh code page through `AcquireCompilationCodePage()`, forwards the NULL runtime into `AcquireCodePageWithCapacity()`, forms `&i_runtime->pagesOpen`, and `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity()` immediately dereferences that invalid pointer, matching the saved MemorySanitizer `SEGV` on a `READ` with crash state `AcquireCodePageWithCapacity -> CompileElseBlock -> Compile_If`. The staged patch adds the missing `if (not o->function)` opcode filter so parser-only expression walking rejects `if` before any code-page allocation path is reached; Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build.

source.description: First project-side materialization point for the vulnerability-relevant state: `Parse_InitExpr()` wraps the attacker-controlled global-initializer bytes in a parser-only `M3Compilation` while leaving `runtime` and `function` NULL.
source.value_from: The saved witness is the 62-byte file `gt_results/arvo_33094/poc` (sha256 `27d9843ed864920ccc007891e5f23e4c87e9fe3672cc5518683e02b82b10aa76`), which starts with wasm magic `00 61 73 6d 01 00 00 00` and then section id `0x06` for the global section. The staged crash stack shows `ParseSection_Global` frame 7 calling `Parse_InitExpr` frame 6 before the later `Compile_BlockStatements -> Compile_If -> CompileElseBlock` crash path.

sink.description: Null-runtime dereference sink. `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity()` performs the faulting read through the invalid list pointer derived from `&NULL->pagesOpen` on the parser-only init-expression path.
sink.note: The saved MemorySanitizer trace reports `SEGV on unknown address 0x000000002988` caused by a `READ memory access`, with frame 0 `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity` and frame 1 `AcquireCodePageWithCapacity /src/wasm3/source/m3_env.c:986:24`. Line 113 is the first dereference in the crashing frame-0 function.

root_cause.description: Missing expression-only opcode restriction lets parser-only `Parse_InitExpr()` dispatch `if` into the normal compiler machinery even though `o->function == NULL` and no runtime/code-page state exists.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (not o->function)` before this dispatch and allows only `i32.const`, `i64.const`, `f32.const`, `f64.const`, `getGlobal`, and `end`; a witness `if` would then hit `default: _throw(m3Err_restictedOpcode)`. The vulnerable source omits that guard and reaches `Compile_If()` instead.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crash stack includes `ParseSection_Global` and `Parse_InitExpr`, so the witness passes wasm header/section dispatch and enters the global-initializer walker that exposes the bug.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement decodes the attacker-controlled initializer bytes into the opcode value that selects the unsafe compiler path. On the crashing path the outer `Compile_BlockStatements()` iteration reads `c_waOp_if`, and a later nested iteration over the same initializer reads `c_waOp_else` and stores it into `o->previousOpcode`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 1 seeded `o->wasm` from the current global initializer inside the 62-byte witness. The staged stack proves these bytes are being consumed under `ParseSection_Global -> Parse_InitExpr -> Compile_BlockStatements` when the crash occurs.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the 62-byte wasm witness directly to `m3_ParseModule()`, and module parsing reaches the global section.
Global-initializer parsing creates a parser-only `M3Compilation` with `runtime == NULL` and `function == NULL`, then hands the initializer bytes to `Compile_BlockStatements()`.

The vulnerable dispatcher reads a disallowed `if` opcode from the initializer and, because it lacks the expression-opcode filter added by the patch, invokes `Compile_If()` instead of rejecting the expression.

While compiling the then arm, the nested `Compile_BlockStatements()` walk later decodes `else`, leaves `o->previousOpcode == c_waOp_else`, and `Compile_If()` enters `CompileElseBlock()` for the else arm.
The else-block allocator path forwards the NULL runtime into the code-page queues, forms `&i_runtime->pagesOpen`, and `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity()` crashes on the resulting invalid read.

fine_trace.note: Source. `Parse_InitExpr()` materializes a parser-only compilation object over the current global initializer. This initializer sets `runtime = NULL`, `module = io_module`, `wasm = *io_bytes`, `wasmEnd = i_end`, and zeroes trailing fields including `function`; the nearby comment says this path should only walk bytes to the terminating `end` without generating code pages.

The initializer bytes are decoded into the opcode value that drives compiler dispatch. On the crashing path this opcode is `c_waOp_if`, not one of the constant-expression opcodes the patch later whitelists.

Root cause. The vulnerable dispatcher goes straight from the decoded opcode to `opinfo->compiler` without checking whether this is a parser-only expression walk. Because step 1 left `o->function == NULL`, a fixed build would reject `opcode == c_waOp_if` with `m3Err_restictedOpcode`; the vulnerable build instead invokes `Compile_If()`.

Inside the nested `CompileBlock()` walk for the then arm, a later `Compile_BlockStatements()` iteration decodes `c_waOp_else` from the same initializer stream. That nested invocation stores the later opcode in `o->previousOpcode` at line 2212 and breaks on `else`, preserving the else-arm marker for `Compile_If()`.

After `CompileBlock()` returns, `Compile_If()` consumes the nested marker from step 4. Because `o->previousOpcode == c_waOp_else` is true, it follows the else-arm path and calls `CompileElseBlock()` instead of resolving the reserved pointer to the current page.

The else-arm compilation path immediately requests a fresh code page. That allocator call receives `o->runtime`, but step 1 established that the parser-only compilation object still has `o->runtime == NULL`.

The NULL runtime is reinterpreted as a real `IM3Runtime` and its `pagesOpen` field address is taken. With `i_runtime == NULL`, this produces the invalid list pointer later dereferenced in `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity`, consistent with the reported low crash address `0x000000002988`.

Sink. `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity()` immediately dereferences the bogus list pointer from step 7, producing the observed `SEGV` on a read. The saved MemorySanitizer trace names `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity` as frame 0 and `AcquireCodePageWithCapacity:986` as frame 1 for this same fault.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved trace crashes in frame 0 `RemoveCodePageOfCapacity`; line 113 is that function's first dereference, and frame 1 `AcquireCodePageWithCapacity:986` is fine-trace step 7 immediately above it.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Frames 2-10 line up with the fine trace and coarse trace: else-block code-page allocation from `Compile_If` under `Parse_InitExpr` reached from `ParseSection_Global` and the fuzz harness.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The same attacker-controlled global-initializer bytes seeded at `Parse_InitExpr` are decoded first as `c_waOp_if` and later, in the nested then-arm walk, as `c_waOp_else` stored in `o->previousOpcode`; that else marker drives `CompileElseBlock()` and the downstream NULL-runtime dereference in the code-page allocator.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `fuzzer` target on `gt_results/arvo_33094/poc`. `m3_ParseModule()` reaches `ParseSection_Global -> Parse_InitExpr`, dispatches a forbidden initializer `if`, the nested then-arm walk later records `else` in `o->previousOpcode`, and the vulnerable parser crashes when else-block compilation tries to acquire a code page through a NULL runtime.

format.name: WebAssembly binary module
format.contract: The verified witness is the staged 62-byte wasm binary whose global-section initializer is walked by `Parse_InitExpr` and whose opcode stream reaches `c_waOp_if` and later `c_waOp_else` while the compilation object still has `runtime == NULL` and `function == NULL`.
